title: Superconducting Logic
description: A computer's bit can be a single quantum of magnetic flux. In rapid single flux quantum logic a Josephson junction flips and lets one flux quantum through, a picosecond pulse that is the bit; it switches near a hundred gigahertz for a hundred thousandth of a transistor's energy. The catch is the cold: every watt at 4 kelvin costs hundreds at the wall, and too small a junction is flipped by its own warmth. Unlocks the Josephson Logic Bench.

puzzle.goal: A pair of electrons carries charge 2q; the flux through a superconducting loop comes in quanta Φ₀. From Planck's constant h, write Φ₀.
puzzle.name: Flux quantum
puzzle.ask: Find Φ₀ in webers with h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ and q = @{q} C.
puzzle.method: The pair wavefunction must come back to itself round the loop: its phase, 2q·Φ/ħ, is a whole number of 2π.
